newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Cricket, lack of sellers to slow Sri Lanka stocks.
newsitem.headline: Cricket, lack of sellers to slow Sri Lanka stocks.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks are seen opening cautiously on Monday as sellers keep away and investors watch the Asia Cup cricket match where Sri Lanka takes on Pakistan in Colombo, brokers said.
"The market closed on Friday on a cautious note as sellers stayed away and that should continue," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena of Ceylinco Stock Brokers.
"Trading should slow down once the match between Sri Lanka and Pakistan gets underway," he added.
Everything comes to a standstill in cricket-crazy Sri Lanka when the World Cup champions take to the field, brokers said.
On Friday, the all share index closed 2.7 points up at 823.4, on turnover of 33.2 million rupees.
"Turnover should be low today too, but the index should move up because buying interest continues," said Prasanna Chandrasekera of brokerage John Keells.
Investors are looking to buy blue chips ahead of the corporate results for the period to June, which are expected to be good and should be out later this month, brokers said.
